newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Narrower jet/gas oil regrade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Narrower jet/gas oil regrade.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread continued to narrow on Friday as physical jet fuel was traded on Thursday at lower levels, while gas oil remained firm, brokers said.

They said gas oil continued to get support from a Singapore trader. The trader also bought large volumes of jet fuel -- the latest being 400,000 barrels on Thursday bringing the total to 1.4 million barrels -- but his recent purchases were done at softer levels.
March regrade was offered at 35 cents per barrel, down 35 cents from Thursday, while April was offered at 30 cents, down 10 cents.
Brokers expect swaps regrade to follow the physical market into negative levels soon, as the region enters a low demand period.
Gas oil swaps were steady in thin morning activity with March bid at $26.50, compared with Thursday's $26.60/$26.80. April was quoted at $25.55/$25.75, up from Thrsday's $25.40/$25.50.
Brokers noted more cargo movements would soon be seen into Hong Kong as supplies there were very low.

But current firm prices would discourage buyers from rushing while Chinese importers would rather wait for the 500,000 tonnes of arbitrage cargoes expected to arrive in Asia from the West within the next two to three weeks to fill up the tanks.
They were hoping that the arbitrage cargoes would be priced at more competitive levels.
Fuel oil swaps also remained unchanged, continuing to be unfazed by a large build in stocks in Singapore.
The swaps market also reflected the quiet physical market which was waiting a clearer direction on market direction.
The naphtha market was quiet in the morning with prices largely unchanged from Thursday.
